findings.summary: The documented 'empty allowlist is identity-neutral, so the default configuration fingerprint is unchanged' claim is not pinned by any test. Removing the empty-allowlist early return in RendererConfigurationFingerprint.AppendAllowedValues (so an empty allowlist contributes a zero count) passes the entire 1499-test suite.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Configuration/RendererConfigurationFingerprint.cs AppendAllowedValues returns early for allowedValues.Count == 0 with the comment that the default configuration fingerprint is unchanged.

tests/ArrTags.Tests/RendererConfigurationTests.cs:532-535 RendererFingerprintIsSensitiveToAllowedValuesAndNormalizesCaseAndOrder asserts Assert.Equal(original, Fingerprint(empty)) where both 'original' (no selector entry) and 'empty' (a Quality entry with an empty AllowedValues) flow through the same empty-list code path, so the assertion is satisfied regardless of the early return.
Mutation M3 (early return removed, empty contributes 'selectorAllowedValueCount=0') -> full suite Failed 0, Passed 1436, Skipped 63, Total 1499: no test failed.

No hardcoded renderer-configuration fingerprint constant exists in tests/ (grep for 64-hex literals found only BundledFontTests hashes), so 'byte-identical to the pre-task value' is not otherwise observable.
findings.recommended_action: Either add a pinned default-fingerprint constant assertion (which task 12.4 will have to update when CurrentSchemaVersion advances to 2 and RenderVersion to 3), or narrow the documented claim to the property the tests actually establish (an explicit empty allowlist is equivalent to an absent allowlist), or explicitly record in docs that the pre-task identity is a deliberate implementation decision not covered by a regression test.

findings.summary: BadgeDefinitionTests.DefinitionRejectsUnusableAllowedValues does not isolate the BadgeDefinition entry-count bound: its too-many input is 33 identical 'value' entries, so the assertion passes via the case-insensitive duplicate rule. Removing the count guard in BadgeDefinition.NormalizeAllowedValues passes all BadgeDefinitionTests.
evidence: tests/ArrTags.Tests/BadgeDefinitionTests.cs DefinitionRejectsUnusableAllowedValues builds tooMany = Enumerable.Repeat("value", BadgeDefinition.MaximumAllowedValues + 1), i.e. 33 identical entries.
src/ArrTags/Rendering/BadgeDefinition.cs NormalizeAllowedValues throws on the second 'value' via seen.Add before the count bound is relevant.
Mutation M5 (entry-count bound removed from NormalizeAllowedValues) -> BadgeDefinitionTests Failed 0, Passed 10, Total 10: no test failed.

The same bound is still genuinely covered at configuration load by ValidatorRejectsTooManyAllowedValues, which uses unique 'value-{index}' entries; mutation M1 (allowlist validation removed) failed that test.
findings.recommended_action: Use distinct entries for the too-many case (for example value-{index}) so the assertion exercises the count bound rather than the duplicate rule. Low impact: the config-load path and the bound are already covered by ValidatorRejectsTooManyAllowedValues.

findings.summary: The settings-page exposure is verified by static substring assertions over the embedded resource, not by a functional populate/save round-trip; the pinned elevation-gated JSON POST deserialization of AllowedValues is not exercised. This matches the pre-existing page-test pattern and the implementation-reviewer 12.1-F4 note.
evidence: tests/ArrTags.Tests/DashboardSettingsPageTests.cs PageExposesAndRoundTripsThePerSelectorAllowlist asserts the eight 'selector-<name>-allowedValues' input ids, 'configured.AllowedValues', and 'AllowedValues: parseAllowedValues' substrings only.
src/ArrTags/Configuration/config.html populateSelectors reads configured.AllowedValues and submit builds AllowedValues: parseAllowedValues(...); parseAllowedValues splits on ',' and trims.
The two host-guarded DashboardSettingsPageTests facts that serve the real pinned DashboardController are skipped without ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR; they do not assert allowlist behavior.
Mutation M6 (removing the UpgradePending allowlist input from config.html) failed PageExposesAndRoundTripsThePerSelectorAllowlist, so the static check is non-vacuous for input presence.
findings.recommended_action: None required for 12.1. The XML round-trip (RendererConfigurationRoundTripsThroughXmlSerializer) covers persistence, and the live POST/page behavior remains owned by task 14.3.

findings.summary: Boundary tests are reject-side only: there is no accepted-at-exactly-32-entries or accepted-at-exactly-64-characters case, and the assertions compare against the BadgeDefinition constants rather than a literal, so the exact numeric bound values are not pinned.
evidence: tests/ArrTags.Tests/RendererConfigurationTests.cs ValidatorRejectsTooManyAllowedValues adds index <= BadgeDefinition.MaximumAllowedValues entries (33) and asserts the error contains the constant; ValidatorRejectsTooLongAllowedValue uses MaximumAllowedValueLength + 1 (65).
No test constructs a definition/configuration with exactly 32 valid unique entries or exactly 64 characters and asserts it is accepted.
findings.recommended_action: None required. This is the common constant-referencing pattern and the bound direction (over-bound rejected) is established; noted only for completeness.

summary: The task 12.1 tests genuinely establish the allowlist configuration, bounds, validation, resolved definition allowlist, fingerprint inclusion, and settings-page exposure. Independent mutation testing on a clean c56d228 worktree confirms non-vacuousness: removing the allowlist validation call fails 9 focused tests; omitting allowlists from the fingerprint or removing case/order normalization each fails RendererFingerprintIsSensitiveToAllowedValuesAndNormalizesCaseAndOrder; removing a settings-page allowlist input fails the page-exposure fact. The focused matrix (50 passed / 2 skipped / 52) and the full default matrix (Failed 0, Passed 1436, Skipped 63, Total 1499) reproduce the reported counts once the package artifact is present; from a clean checkout the same revision is 1433/66/1499 because three unrelated packaging facts skip. No new skips were introduced and the two host-guarded DashboardSettingsPageTests facts are pre-existing and hide no allowlist behavior. Two LOW findings remain, both narrow: the 'empty allowlist is identity-neutral / default fingerprint unchanged' claim survives a full-suite mutation (M3) because the test compares two configurations that share the same empty-list code path, and the BadgeDefinition entry-count assertion is masked by its duplicate input (M5). Neither affects the task 12.1 acceptance criteria (bounded, validated, secret-free allowlist whose change alters the fingerprint), which are established. PASS_WITH_FINDINGS; ready for the next task.
